newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat closes lower on corn/soy drop, hedging.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat closes lower on corn/soy drop, hedging.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed lower on a drop in CBOT corn and soybean futures, hedge selling and a technical slip, traders said.
"Technically it was a pretty poor performance and the market is set up to break another eight to 10 cents," a trader said.

The market remained enamored with the trend in corn and soybeans amid a volatile U.S. weather market. There were early calls for corn and soy to be strongly higher but forecasts for wetter weather later this week in the Midwest triggered a selloff and those markets ended lower.
Dry weather in the central and southern portion of the U.S. Midwest corn/soy growing region had led to calls for strong gains in CBOT corn and soybean futures prices.

KCBT September wheat early moved fractions above the top of a chart gap of $3.73 to $3.74-1/2 then faltered, a scenario that tilted the market into a technical downturn. The session high for September was $3.75.
KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed four to 5-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with September down 4-1/4 at $3.64-1/4.
The market took in stride news the Australian Wheat Board reduced by one million tonnes to between 14 million to 15 million tonnes its estimate for Australia's 1997-98 wheat crop.
"We've known it was dry in Australia so it didn't surprise anyone," a trader said referring to the Australian wheat crop estimate.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the KCBT at 42,060 contracts, above the 31,875 traded Friday.
